paragraphs: Friend, somebody asks Jesus whether only a few will be saved, and He doesn't give a head count. He says, "Make every effort to enter through the narrow door." (Luke 13:24) So the question stops being about everybody else and becomes about you. I think Jesus cares more about where you're standing than about what the crowd is doing.

Now look at the people knocking. They bring up eating and drinking with Him and hearing Him teach in their streets, and the door stays shut. (Luke 13:25-27) Being near Jesus is not the same as knowing Him, like standing in my bakery all day and calling yourself a cookie. Meanwhile, people come from east and west and north and south to recline at the table in the kingdom of God, and some who are last will be first, so the invitation reaches far past the people you'd expect. (Luke 13:29-30)

Then look at Jesus' heart. The Pharisees warn Him about Herod, and He keeps right on going toward Jerusalem. (Luke 13:31-33) He cries out to the city, "how often I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!" (Luke 13:34) That's not a cold door-slammer talking, friend, that's someone with open wings who wants everybody in, so come in through the door while it's open.
